parsed.main_gap: The key Lemma (for every term x, the set of prime divisors of x that are at most a_1 already meets the support of every term) is asserted with proof 'standard; details omitted'. This is the entire difficulty of the problem.

errors.description: The Lemma is the heart of the proof: it is what allows replacing the infinite prime-support constraint family by the finitely many primes ≤ a_1. No argument is given; the 'Rp^k construction' alluded to later is never carried out. Without it, equivalence (3), periodicity (4), and the conclusion all rest on an unproved claim.
errors.quote: **Proof.** Induction over the sequence terms in increasing order (standard; details omitted). \(\square\)

errors.description: Section 4, item 4 mentions a strategy ('The construction \(Rp^k\) repairs this boundary issue') but this is a description of an intended approach, not a proof; it earns no credit.
errors.quote: The construction \(Rp^k\) repairs this boundary issue while preserving exactly the small-prime support; the lemma proves the strengthened hypothesis.

parsed.notes: Correct and easy parts: unboundedness with gaps ≤ a_1, characterization (1) of terms via good supports, and the deduction of a_{n+T}=a_n+L from periodicity of the term set modulo L. These are a reduction with the main argument absent. Computational evidence and self-checks earn nothing.
